newsitem.title: USA: US rate fears prompt corporate debt issuer rush.
newsitem.headline: US rate fears prompt corporate debt issuer rush.

text.p: Fears that strong U.S. economic data this week will trigger the Federal Reserve Board to tighten credit again, has issuers rushing to finance debt now, rather than later, dealers said.
"We've seen some new names added to this week's business...issuers are trying to head off the possibility of higher interest rates," one high-grade syndicate source said.

One newcomer is General Motors Corp'S, financing arm General Motors Acceptance Corp (GMAC), which is expected to issue $500 million in A3/A-minus rated four-year noncallabe notes. Lehman Brothers is expected to underwrite the deal.
Price talk on a four-year deal from General Motors Corp's GMAC unit is 40 basis points over the 6-1/2 percent U.S. Treasury note due 2001, sources said.

"Fears that this week's load of economic data will push the Fed to hike rates again has everyone trying to square away business," said another syndicate source. "Nobody expected GMAC to come in with a $500 million issue."

Another new name that has emerged is Dominion Resources, sources said. The firm is expected to set $800 million in Baa1/A-minus rated debt offering consisting of five and 10-year debt via underwriter Lehman Brothers, they said.

The rush to finance debt, despite already higher financing rates, comes amid this week's heavy supply of U.S. economic indicators. They include: durable goods, the employment cost index, consumer confidence, NAPM, first quarter GDP and nonfarm payrolls/unemployment data.

Stronger-than-expected reports would heighten fears that the Fed's policy-setting arm, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will tighten credit again at its next meeting on May 20. The FOMC voted last month to raise the key federal funds overnight lending rate by 1/4 point, making it more costly for U.S. corporations to finance debt.
Among other names in the market are Briggs & Stratton Corp's $175 million five and 10-year debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Sunlife Canada is also slated to bring $500 million of a step-up offering one day this week, sources said.
Also, Bank United Corp is expected to set $220 million in debt.
Meanwhile, CSX Corp is also slated to bring $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering via underwriters Salomon Brothers, Credit Suisse First Boston and Chase Securities.
The deal is expected to include five-year, seven-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches, in addition to a 30-year trust preferred issue, sources said.
Last week, the corporate bond primary market saw about $6.0 billion in new straight debt issuance, dealers said.
Norfolk Southern Corp was expected to issue between $3.0 - $4.0 billion next week in a debt offering via joint lead managers Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan Securities.

Among upcoming high-yield issues, Pride Petroleum Services Inc was expected to sell $300 million in 10-year senior notes later this week via lead underwriter Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. The issue has a three-year equity call for $100 million, sources said.
Colorado Prime Corp was expected to set $100 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via JP Morgan Securities.
Another $85 million in 10-year 144A notes was expected to come from HCC Industries Inc.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 1/32 at 93-21/32 to yield 7.14 percent.
